Surat al-Mulk (The Sovereignty) is Meccan, and its verses number thirty.

﴿Blessed is He﴾ (tabaraka), exalted above the attributes of created beings (al-muhaddithin), ﴿in whose hand is﴾ (bi-yadihi), in His disposal (fi tasarrufihi), ﴿the dominion﴾ (al-mulk), meaning sovereignty (al-sultan) and power (al-qudra).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 2:

﴿Who created death and life﴾ — death in this world and life in the Hereafter; or both are in this world, for the drop of semen is subject to life, which is that by which one perceives, and death is its opposite, or its absence; there are two opinions. And "created" on the second view means "decreed."

﴿That He may test you﴾ — that He may examine you regarding life, ﴿as to which of you is best in deed﴾ — most obedient to Allah. ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ — in His retribution against whoever disobeys Him, ﴿the Oft-Forgiving﴾ — toward whoever repents to Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 3:

﴿The One who created seven heavens in layers﴾, one above another, without contact between them. ﴿You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any disproportion﴾, whether in them or in other things. ﴿Disproportion﴾ means discord and lack of harmony. ﴿So return your gaze﴾ — repeat it — ﴿towards the sky﴾. ﴿Do you see any rifts﴾ in it, ﴿any fissures or cracks﴾?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 4:

﴿Then return your gaze twice﴾, one time after another, ﴿and your gaze will return to you⁠ ⁠﴾ coming back, ﴿humbled﴾ abased, due to not perceiving any flaw, ﴿while it is fatigued﴾ worn out from seeing any flaw.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 5:

﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven﴾ the nearer one to the earth, ﴿with lamps﴾ with stars, ﴿and We have made them missiles﴾ means of stoning ﴿against the devils﴾ when they try to eavesdrop, by a flaming fire separating from the star, like a brand taken from the fire, which strikes the jinn and kills him or injures him, not that the star itself moves from its place. ﴿And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾ the kindled fire.
﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and what an evil destination it is.﴾ هِيَ

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 7:

﴿When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring (shahiq), while it boils up﴾ (sawtan munkaran ka-sawt al-himar, "a hideous sound like the braying of a donkey") ﴿and it seethes﴾ (taghli, "it boils")

﴿Almost bursting﴾, and it is read as ﴿تَتَمَيَّز﴾ (tatamayyaz) in the original form, meaning "tearing apart", ﴿with rage﴾, meaning anger at the disbelievers. ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it﴾, meaning a group of them, ﴿its keepers ask them﴾, as a rebuke: ﴿Did there not come to you a warner?﴾, meaning a messenger who would warn you of the punishment of God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 9:

﴿They will say, "Yes, indeed, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'"﴾ It is possible that this is the speech of the angels to the disbelievers when they are informed of the denial, and it is possible that it is the speech of the disbelievers to the warners.

ﷻ "And they will say, 'If only we had listened or reasoned...'" (Q. 67:10). The Jalalayn comments:

﴿And they said: "Had we but listened"﴾ i.e., listening with understanding, ﴿"or reasoned"﴾ i.e., reasoning with reflection.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 11:**

﴿So they will confess﴾ when confession will not benefit them, ﴿to their sin﴾, which is their denying the warner. ﴿Then, away with them﴾, with the letter ﺡ in ﴿فَسُحْقًا﴾ read both with sukun (*suhqan*) and with damma (*suhuqan*), ﴿the companions of the Blaze﴾. So, far away from them is the mercy of God.

Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen (﴿إنّ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبّهمْ﴾ يَخافُونَهُ ﴿بِالغَيْبِ﴾) — that is, they fear Him — ﴿unseen﴾ in their absence from the eyes of people, so they obey Him in secret, and so their obedience in the open is more fitting. ﴿For them there is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ — that is, Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 13:

﴿And keep your speech secret, O people, or make it public; indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [Meaning: He is Exalted, Knowing of what is within the breasts, of what is in them; so how much more of what you utter.] The occasion of revelation of this is that some of the polytheists said to others: "Keep your speech secret, lest the God of Muhammad hear you."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 14:

﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ what you conceal; that is, can His knowledge of that be negated? ﴿And He is the Subtle [al-Latif], the Acquainted [al-Khabir]﴾ in His knowledge ﴿the Acquainted﴾ with it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 15:

﴿He is the One who made the earth subservient to you﴾ easy (sahla) for walking in it ﴿so walk in its shoulders﴾ its sides ﴿and eat of His provision﴾ the created things for your sake ﴿and to Him is the resurrection﴾ from the graves for the recompense.

﴿Are you secure﴾ with the two hamzas (أأمنتم) pronounced as two full hamzas (tahqiq), or with the second softened (tashil), and with an alif inserted between them and between the second and the following letter, or with that alif omitted, or with the second hamza replaced by an alif (ibdal).

﴿from He who is in the heaven﴾, meaning His authority and His power, ﴿that He should cause the earth to swallow you﴾. Here "an yakhsif" (أن يخسف) is a badal (substitute, i.e., grammatical apposition) for "man" (من), ﴿with you, and behold, it shakes﴾, meaning it moves with you and rises above you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 17:

﴿Or do you feel secure from He who is in the heaven that He will send against you a storm of stones?﴾ "Who is in the heaven" is a substitute (badal) for "He who" (man). ﴿A storm of stones﴾: a wind that pelts you with pebbles. ﴿Then you will know﴾ at the moment of witnessing the punishment ﴿how was My warning﴾, i.e., My warning of the punishment, meaning that it is true.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 18:

﴿And indeed, those before them denied [the truth], from among the nations﴾ ﴿so how was My disapproval?﴾ — i.e., how was My rejection of them, through [their] denial, when I destroyed them? It means that it was indeed [justified].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 19:

﴿Have they not seen﴾ (yanzuru) look at ﴿the birds above them﴾ in the air ﴿spreading their wings﴾ outstretched, ﴿and folding them in﴾ their wings after spreading them, meaning and folding them (wa-qabidat) ﴿but the Most Merciful upholds them﴾ from falling while spreading and folding ﴿by His power﴾ ﴿Indeed He is Seeing of all things﴾. The meaning: Have they not reflected on the birds remaining in the air as evidence of Our power to do to them what We did before and other punishment?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 20:

﴿Amman﴾ (ﷻ) is a subject (mubtada'), ﴿hadha﴾ is its predicate (khabar), ﴿alladhi﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿hadha﴾, ﴿huwa jund﴾ means helpers (a'wan) ﴿lakum﴾ is a relative clause (silah) of ﴿alladhi﴾, ﴿yansurukum﴾ is a descriptive clause (sifah) of ﴿jund﴾, ﴿min dun al-Rahman﴾ means other than the Most Merciful, i.e., one who would repel His punishment from you, meaning you have no helper. ﴿In﴾ means "what" (ma), ﴿al-kafirun illa fi ghurur﴾ means the disbelievers are only in delusion; Satan has deceived them into thinking that punishment will not descend upon them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 21:

﴿Or who is it that will provide for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ (The Most Merciful) ﴿His provision﴾, i.e., the rain, from you. The response of the conditional is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e., "then who will provide for you?", meaning there is no provider for you besides Him. ﴿Rather, they persist﴾ (tamadaw, continued stubbornly) ﴿in arrogance﴾ (takabbur, pride) ﴿and aversion﴾ (tabaʿud, distancing themselves from the truth).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 22:

﴿Is he who walks prostrate, falling on his face, better guided, or he who walks upright on a straight path?﴾ (Upright, moderate) ﴿on a straight path﴾ (a path, a way) ﴿straight﴾. The predicate of the second clause is omitted, and it is indicated by the predicate of the first, i.e., "better guided." And the parable is about the believer and the disbelievers: which of them is upon guidance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 23:

﴿Say: He it is Who brought you into being⁠⁠⁠⁠ and made for you hearing, sight and hearts⁠⁠⁠⁠,⁠⁠⁠⁠ little are you grateful.⁠⁠⁠⁠﴾ "Brought you into being" means created you. "And made for you hearing, sight and hearts" means the hearts (al-af'idah). "Little are you grateful" — mā is extra (mazīdah), and the sentence is a new, independent clause (mustaʼnafah) informing that their gratitude for these blessings is extremely little.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 24:

﴿Say: It is He who created you (dhara'akum) on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered﴾ (khalaqakum) ﴿on the earth and to Him you will be gathered﴾ for the reckoning.

Note on the text as given: the commentary's gloss on the verse's opening words is rendered above as "created you," and the gloss on the second clause as "for the reckoning."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 25:

﴿And they say﴾ to the believers, ﴿"When is this promise?"﴾ the promise of gathering (al-hashr), ﴿"if you are truthful"﴾ regarding it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 26:

﴿Say, "Knowledge [of when it will come] is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."﴾ [The knowledge of its coming] is with Allah; I am only a manifest warner, one whose warning is clear.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 27:

﴿When they see it﴾, i.e., the punishment after the gathering, ﴿approaching﴾, near, ﴿the faces of those who disbelieved will be blackened﴾, i.e., will turn black. ﴿And it will be said﴾, i.e., the guardians of the Fire will say to them, ﴿This is what you used to call for﴾, i.e., the punishment, ﴿by its warning﴾, ﴿that you denied﴾, that you would not be resurrected. This is a narration of a future situation, expressed in the past tense to affirm that it will certainly occur.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 28:

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah destroys me and those with me of the believers with His punishment, as you wish for us, or has mercy on us, then who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"﴾ That is, there is no protector for them from it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 67, verse 29:**

﴿Say, "He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him, and in Him we have put our trust. So you will come to know"﴾ with the *tā'* (تاء, addressing "you") and the *yā'* (ياء, "they"), at the witnessing of the punishment, ﴿who is in manifest error﴾, clear, whether it is we, you, or they.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 67, verse 30:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if your water should become sunken into the earth,﴾ sunk deep within the earth, ﴿then who will bring you flowing water?﴾ flowing, which can be reached by hands and buckets, like your water; meaning, none brings it except Allah the Exalted. So how can you deny that He will resurrect you?

It is recommended that the reciter say after ﴿flowing water﴾: "Allah, Lord of the worlds," as has been reported in the hadith. This verse was recited in the presence of some tyrants, and one of them said: "Axes and hoes will bring it!" So the water of his eye departed and he went blind. We seek refuge in Allah from audacity toward Allah and toward His signs.
